  description: 'Public workspace: /mnt/raid/home/yangshuangning/vuln_variant_search/experiments/clairvoyant_variant_search/runs/10_cluster/C2/public. Seed: mptcp: Fix out of bounds when parsing TCP options. The full public demonstration is in seed.json. Snapshot IDs: s01, s02, s03'
- id: goal
  description: Search every independent snapshot for credible variants of the seed's root-cause mechanism; preserve exact source evidence and resolve every promising candidate.
- id: f001
  description: 'MECHANISM PROFILE (seed: mptcp_get_options TCP-option walk OOB read; demo only, never reportable). Untrusted source: remotely attacker-controlled bytes forming a variable-length option/TLV chain inside a packet header (TCP options of an incoming segment; generally any packet-derived TLV/IE buffer). Missing guarantee: the parser loop consumes a discriminator/opcode byte and adjusts its remaining-length bookkeeping, but never enforces the invariant that at least 2 bytes remain before dereferencing the next byte as the field-size (opsize); pointer advance and length bookkeeping diverge from the true buffer bounds. Unsafe use/state transition: with remaining==1 the loop reads the opcode, then executes ''opsize = *ptr++'' past the end of the option area; sibling shapes read a size byte but then use it without clamping to remaining bytes, driving larger over-reads or memcpy overruns. Security-relevant consequence: out-of-bounds read of packet-adjacent memory (info leak / KASAN-detectable crash), plus potential wider OOB reads/copies from an unvalidated size field. Canonical fix shape: guard ''if (length < 2) return'' before each dependent read, and clamp any size field to remaining length before copying/advancing. BRANCHES: branch1=tcp-optwalk-len2=audit every in-tree TCP-option walk (net/ipv4/tcp_input.c tcp_parse_options and its callers, net/ipv6/syncookies.c, net/mptcp sub-option loops, net/dccp option parsing, TCP MD5/AO/fastopen option handling) for a missing remaining>=2 check between consuming the kind byte and reading the length byte, including off-by-one bookkeeping in the EOL/NOP fast path; branch2=ip-exthdr-tlv-walk=audit IP-layer variable-length header walkers (IPv4 IPOPT loops, IPv6 hop-by-hop/destination-option and other exthdr TLV iteration in net/ipv6, IP-option helpers in net/core) for the same step: consume a type byte then read a length byte without confirming 2 bytes remain, or advance the cursor by an unvalidated element length; branch3=l2-wireless-ie-tlv=audit L2/wireless information-element and TLV parsers (cfg80211/mac80211 802.11 IE walks, radiotap, Bluetooth EIR/AD/SDP/AMP attribute loops) where an element-id byte is consumed and the length byte or body is read when fewer than 2 bytes remain, or traversal advances by an unvalidated element length; branch4=optsize-body-clamp=audit network option parsers that read a size byte but use it unclamped: memcpy, pointer advance, or get_unaligned of ''size'' bytes without a ''size <= remaining'' guard, so a truncated final option over-reads past the buffer end.'
- id: f002
  description: |-
    artifact=/mnt/raid/home/yangshuangning/vuln_variant_search/experiments/clairvoyant_variant_search/runs/10_cluster/C2/agent-state/findings/i005.json; branch=ip-exthdr-tlv-walk; snapshots=s01; missing=s02,s03; findings=2; unresolved=0; execution_status=complete
    finding 1: s01:net/ipv6/exthdrs.c:140-148 confidence=low; source quote='while (len > 0) { int optlen = nh[off + 1] + 2;'; reason=ip6_parse_tlv() (used by ipv6_destopt_rcv and ipv6_rthdr_rcv for hop-by-hop/destination options of remotely received IPv6 packets) walks attacker-controlled TLV bytes: at loop entry with len==1 it reads the type byte nh[off] via the switch and then dereferences nh[off + 1] as the option length with no 'len >= 2' check between consuming the type byte and reading the length byte - structurally identical to the seed mptcp_get_options OOB (the 'optlen > len' clamp only happens later, in the default case, after the length byte is already read). Whether this is a real OOB depends on whether nh[off+1] lies inside the linear data area: the caller does pskb_may_pull() of the full hdrlen before ip6_parse_tlv(), so hdrlen bytes ending at skb_transport_offset+hdrlen are linear; when len==1 the final TLV ends exactly at that boundary, making nh[off+1] read one byte past the pulled header region and potentially past the skb linear length for a packet whose option header ends exactly at the end of linear data. Exploitability is unproven (the byte is usually within the skb head allocation), hence low confidence, but the missing remaining>=2 guard is exactly the invariant the seed fixed.
    finding 2: s01:net/bridge/br_netfilter_ipv6.c:64-67 confidence=low; source quote='while (len > 0) { int optlen = nh[off + 1] + 2;'; reason=br_nf_check_hbh_len() (bridge netfilter IPv6 validation of forwarded hop-by-hop headers, untrusted input on any bridged port) has the same shape: when len==1 the switch reads the type byte nh[off] (IPV6_TLV_PAD1 case sets optlen=1, but IPV6_TLV_PADN falls through and every other type hits the default case) and 'int optlen = nh[off + 1] + 2' has already dereferenced nh[off+1] before any remaining>=2 check; the only guard, 'if ((raw + len) - skb->data > skb_headlen(skb)) goto bad', bounds the header extent but does not guarantee two bytes remain for the final TLV. Same seed-equivalent missing invariant; impact bounded similarly (reads within/just past the linear skb region), hence low confidence.
    candidate: s01:net/ipv6/exthdrs.c:141 status=reported; ip6_parse_tlv reads nh[off + 1] as optlen source without a remaining>=2 check; PAD1 is handled but PADN and default-path options consume the length byte when len==1; reported as low-confidence variant of the seed mechanism.
    candidate: s01:net/bridge/br_netfilter_ipv6.c:65 status=reported; br_nf_check_hbh_len reads nh[off + 1] + 2 with only a whole-header headlen bound; no per-TLV remaining>=2 check before the length byte; reported as low-confidence variant.
    candidate: s01:net/ipv4/ip_options.c:286 status=safe; ip_options_compile has the canonical fixed shape: explicit 'if (unlikely(l < 2)) { pp_ptr = optptr; goto error; }' before reading optlen = optptr[1], plus 'optlen < 2 || optlen > l' clamp (lines 286-294).
    candidate: s01:net/ipv6/exthdrs_core.c:133 status=safe; ipv6_find_tlv pre-checks 'if (offset + 2 > packet_len) goto bad' before entering the loop, reads the type byte only inside the loop with that bound, and clamps 'if (optlen > len) goto bad' after reading nh[offset+1]; the length-byte read happens only when offset+2 <= packet_len was established for the current iteration's start. ipv6_skip_exthdr and ipv6_find_hdr use skb_header_pointer for every header fetch.
    candidate: s01:net/ipv6/calipso.c:834 status=safe; calipso_tlv_len checks 'if (offset + 1 >= opt_len) return -EINVAL' before reading tlv[offset + 1] and 'if (offset + tlv_len > opt_len) return -EINVAL' after; both calipso_opt_find (line 875) and the sock_getattr walker (line 1105) route every step through it.
    candidate: s01:net/ipv6/netfilter/ip6t_hbh.c:117 status=safe; hbh_mt6 checks 'if (hdrlen < 1) break' before fetching the type byte and 'if (hdrlen < 2) break' before fetching the length byte, both through skb_header_pointer which cannot over-read; the optlen advance is additionally guarded by 'ptr > skb->len - optlen || hdrlen < optlen'.
    candidate: s01:net/ipv6/ah6.c:127 status=safe; zero_out_mutable_opts and ipv6_rearrange_destopt both contain 'if (len < 2) goto bad' before reading opt[off+1] and 'if (len < optlen) goto bad' before advancing (lines 127-145 and 171-190).
    limitation: The two reported candidates are structural matches only: no runtime reproducer or KASAN confirmation was built, and the byte read may in most packet layouts still fall inside the skb linear area, so actual out-of-bounds impact is unproven (expressed as low confidence).
    limitation: Remaining IPv6 exthdr walkers identified but not deeply read: net/ipv6/mip6.c and net/ipv6/output_core.c (ipv6_find_tlv callers), net/ipv6/netfilter/ip6t_rt.c (routing-header type-0 hop walk), net/ipv6/netfilter/ip6t_srh.c, net/ipv6/seg6.c (SRH processing), net/ipv6/exthdrs_offload.c, and net/ipv6/exthdrs.c ipv6_rthdr_rcv/seg6 helpers.
    limitation: ip6_parse_tlv PADN path also performs 'for (i = 2; i < optlen; i++) nh[off + i]' reads gated only by the implicit header-extent pull, not by a per-option clamp; not separately validated.
    limitation: No dynamic analysis (KASAN/syzkaller harness) was run because the snapshot is a read-only source tree without build configuration; conclusions are from line-level reading of the complete loop bodies and their callers' pskb_may_pull preconditions.
